overview.description: Púkk (often spelled 'Pukk') is a traditional Icelandic card game that belongs to the ancient 'Poch' family. It involves a unique betting layout (traditionally a series of dishes or a special mat) and three distinct phases of play: Dressing the Board, Vying (the 'Púkk' phase), and Shedding (the 'Play' phase). It is famous for its 'Pamfíll' (Jack of Clubs) which acts as a powerful wild card. Púkk is a game of social interaction, bluffing, and sequence-building that has been an Icelandic family staple for centuries.

history.origins: Derived from the 15th-century German game 'Pochen' and the French 'Poque'. It arrived in Iceland and evolved into its current form with localized terminology and the specific 'Pamfíll' mechanic.
timeline: 1800s: Púkk becomes the definitive social game in Icelandic coastal villages.
1950s: Modern layout mats are produced commercially in Reykjavik.
Present: Remains a core 'Hygge' game for Christmas and social gatherings in Iceland.
history.evolution: The removal of 2s, 3s, and 4s was a deliberate change to make sequences (the final phase) faster and more high-stakes.
history.cultural: Names for the positions: 'Ás' (Ace), 'Kongur' (King), 'Drottning' (Queen), 'Gosi' (Jack), 'Tía' (Ten), and 'Pamfíll' (Jack of Clubs).

setup.equipment: 40-card pack, Púkk betting layout (mat or set of dishes/pools), chips.

rules.objective: Win the chips in the compartments by having specific cards or winning the betting phase.
rules.gameplay: Each game has four stages: (1) Dressing the board—each player places one chip in each of the seven compartments (Ás, Kongur, Drottning, Gosi, Tía, Pamfíll, and central Púkk). (2) Collecting the ante—the turned card designates trump; holders of the Ace, King, Queen, Jack or Ten of trump collect the corresponding pool; the holder of Pamfíll (Jack of Clubs) collects that pool (and both if clubs are trump). (3) Að Púkka—in turn, each player may add a chip to the Púkk compartment to enter; Pamfíll is wild for hand ranking; hands are five of a kind, four, three, or pair (sixes beat Aces); wagering one chip at a time until two remain or no raises; showdown and highest hand wins the Púkk pot. (4) Playing out the hand—shedding: left of dealer leads; players follow with same suit one rank higher until Ace or no one can follow; last to play in a sequence starts the next; first to empty hand wins; others pay one chip per card left.
keyRules: You must have at least a pair of 5s to enter the Púkk (vying) phase; bluffing is illegal.
In the shedding phase, play same suit one rank higher; the last card of a sequence starts the next.
Pamfíll (Jack of Clubs) is wild only in the vying phase; in shedding it is a normal Jack of Clubs.

strategy.basic: Don't bluff! In traditional Púkk rules, it is actually illegal to 'Púkk' without at least a pair. However, you can 'Soft-Púkk' by betting small with a medium pair to induce others to fold. Prioritize the 'Pamfíll' for the Vying phase, but remember it has no special power in the Playing phase—use it as a normal Jack of Clubs to continue a sequence.
strategy.intermediate: Bowl Farming: Pay attention to which bowls have the most chips. If the 'Ace' bowl hasn't been emptied for 5 rounds, it will be huge. If you hold an Ace, your primary goal in the Play phase should be to maneuver the sequence in that suit so that YOU get to play the Ace. This might mean keeping a 10 and Queen of that suit so you can jump in when someone plays the Jack.
strategy.advanced: Sequence Starvation: If you are the leader of a sequence, try to 'Kill' the suit as fast as possible by playing cards that gap the sequence (though you must follow rank if someone else has it). In the Play phase, if you hold the Pamfíll (Jack of Clubs), you know exactly where that Jack is. Use this knowledge to stop sequences in the Club suit effectively.
tips: Sixes beat Aces in the Púkk hand ranking (not the Play ranking). This is a common point of confusion for beginners.
If the board is 'Dressed' but not won, the chips carry over—be more aggressive when the pots are 'Fat'.

difficulty.easy: Fails to 'Dress' the board; misses bowl-claim opportunities; wastes Pamfíll.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable vying bets; understands Púkk ranking; standard sequence play.
difficulty.hard: Expert 'Sequence Controller'; perfectly calculates bowl-probability; uses Pamfíll with 100% efficiency in vying.

phases.label: Dressing the Board
phases.notes: Each player places one chip in each of the seven compartments.

phases.label: Collecting the Ante
phases.notes: Holders of trump Ace/King/Queen/Jack/Ten and Pamfíll collect the corresponding pools.

phases.label: Að Púkka (Vying)
phases.notes: Enter by adding a chip; then wager one chip at a time until two remain or no raises.

phases.label: Showdown
phases.notes: All in the vying show hands; highest Púkk hand wins the Púkk compartment.

phases.label: Playing out the Hand
phases.notes: Same suit one rank higher until stop; last in sequence starts next; first to empty hand wins.

ante.description: Place one chip in each of the seven compartments (Ás, Kongur, Drottning, Gosi, Tía, Pamfíll, and central Púkk) to dress the board.
ante.constraints: Each player must place one chip per compartment at the start of each game.

deal.reason: Deal is performed by the dealer; not a player action.

reveal_market.reason: This game does not use a market to reveal.

buy_market.reason: This game has no market purchase.

buy_stock.reason: This game has no buying from stock.

fold.description: Drop out of the Púkk vying; you no longer participate in the current pot and do not show your hand.
fold.constraints: Legal only during the vying phase when it is your turn.

check.description: Decline to add a chip when it is your turn in the vying phase; you remain in the contest.
check.constraints: Legal when no chip has been added this round or when you do not wish to raise.

call.description: Match the current bet by adding one chip to the Púkk compartment.
call.constraints: Legal during vying when another player has added a chip and you wish to stay in.

bet.description: Add one chip to the Púkk compartment to enter the vying or to raise the stakes.
bet.constraints: To enter you must have at least a pair of 5s; wagering is one chip at a time.

raise.description: Add one chip to the Púkk compartment to raise the current stake.
raise.constraints: Legal during vying when you are in the contest; when only two remain, either may demand showdown.

declare.reason: This game has no declare phase.

reveal_hand.description: Show your Púkk combination to all players; highest hand wins the Púkk compartment.
reveal_hand.constraints: All players still in the vying reveal simultaneously at showdown.

award_pot.reason: This game has no pot to award.

play_card.description: Play a card: either the same suit one rank higher than the last card played, or start a new sequence (if you played the last card of the previous sequence).
play_card.constraints: In the shedding phase you must follow with same suit and next rank when possible; the last player in a sequence may lead any card.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.reason: This game has no pass action.

bid.reason: This game has no bid action.

meld.reason: This game has no meld action.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

wildcards.restrictions: Vying phase only; in shedding phase Pamfíll is a normal Jack of Clubs.

validPlays.notes: Same suit, one rank higher than last card; last in sequence may lead any card to start the next.

shedding.burnRules: Last card played in a sequence (Ace or a stop) allows that player to lead any card to start the next sequence.

customActions.description: Display your card and collect the chips from the corresponding compartment (trump Ace, King, Queen, Jack, or Ten; or Pamfíll pool; if clubs are trump and you hold Pamfíll you collect both).
customActions.constraints: You must hold the card that matches the compartment; the turned card designates trump.

engine.handRankingSystem: Púkk ranking for vying: five of a kind, four of a kind, three of a kind, pair; within category sixes beat Aces, then Aces beat Kings down to 5s; combinations using Pamfíll (wild) beat natural ones.
engine.deckDescription: A 40-card stripped deck: four French suits with ranks 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace (or equivalent). Pukk is an Icelandic Poch variant; betting and board layout phases; trump and trick play follow Poch family rules; 40 cards are used.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each have ten cards in the stripped deck. Trump is determined by the game phase; that suit outranks others; following suit is required when able in tricks.
engine.rankDescription: Ranks 9 through Ace (and possibly 8) in the 40-card strip; in trump, rank order may follow Poch (e.g. Jack high). Trick order and point values follow Icelandic Poch; the highest of the led suit wins unless trumped.
